title: Higher module direct images commute with etale restriction on spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and suppose $g$ is etale. Put $X'=X\times_YY'$, with projections $h:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Use the small etale ringed topoi and module direct images of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For any sheaf $M$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and any integer $q\geq0$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$ (R^qf_*M)|_{Y'}\;\cong\;R^qf'_*(M|_{X'}). $$
Here higher direct images are the right derived functors of module direct image, computed by injective resolutions in the categories of all module sheaves. The restrictions are tensor pullbacks along $g$ and $h$, equivalently restrictions to the localized etale sites [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. There is no quasi-coherence, properness or Noetherian assumption.

proof.text: Present each small etale module category by the enlarged etale ringed site $\mathcal C_Z$ of algebraic-space objects, chosen small in a common larger sheaf universe. The enlarged-site-model statement identifies the topoi, structure sheaves and module categories, and identifies an etale map with localization. The degree-zero restriction statement identifies both $g^*$ and $h^*$ with these module restrictions. The etale map $g$ is representable etale in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space], and it is chartwise etale: for a representable etale map $U\to Y'$ from a scheme and a scheme $T\to Y$, the fibre product $T\times_YU=(T\times_YY')\times_{Y'}U$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is a scheme etale over the scheme $T\times_YY'$, which is etale over $T$, so $U\to Y$ is representable etale. Hence $h$ is chartwise etale by the arbitrary-base-change clause of the chartwise-etale-permanence statement applied to $g$ and $f$; it is also representable etale, since $T\times_XX'=T\times_YY'$ for every scheme $T\to X$. No surjectivity of $g$ is needed. The exact localized-module adjunction therefore makes both restrictions exact and supplies an exact left adjoint $j_!$ to each restriction. No scheme presentation for $Y'$ itself is required.

proof.text: Apply the right-adjoint-preserves-injectives statement to the exact functor $j_!$ left adjoint to $h^*$. Thus $h^*$ preserves injective module sheaves. This is preservation in the categories of modules over the restricted structure sheaf; no claim that arbitrary module pullback preserves injectives is used.

proof.text: On the small ringed-site presentations the category of modules is Grothendieck abelian by the ringed-site resolution-existence statement. Hence it has enough injectives by the Grothendieck-enough-injectives statement. The injective-resolution existence statement gives $M\to I^\bullet$ with $I^r=0$ for $r<0$. By Steps 1 and 2, $h^*M\to h^*I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution: exactness preserves the augmented exact sequence, and each $h^*I^r$ is injective. These facts apply also to the target module categories. The direct-image functors are the additive right adjoints of the tensor-pullback adjunction, hence preserve finite limits and are left exact.

proof.text: Write $\beta_N:g^*f_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}f'_*h^*N$ for the cited ordinary module comparison. Apply it to $N=I^r$ in each degree. Naturality for $d^r:I^r\to I^{r+1}$ says $f'_*h^*(d^r)\circ\beta_{I^r}=\beta_{I^{r+1}}\circ g^*f_*(d^r)$, so these maps give an isomorphism of complexes $\beta_I:g^*f_*I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}f'_*h^*I^\bullet$. They are maps of $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-modules because the cited comparison is the identity on compatible chart sections with their restricted scalar action.

source.place: Tag 03LX, lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules; apply the ordinary comparison in the injective-resolution argument of Tag 03LR

proof.text: The resolution comparison for right derived functors computes $R^qf_*M$ as $H^q(f_*I^\bullet)$ and $R^qf'_*(h^*M)$ as $H^q(f'_*h^*I^\bullet)$, using the resolution from Step 3. Exactness of $g^*$ and the exact-functor cohomology statement give the canonical isomorphism $g^*H^q(f_*I^\bullet)\cong H^q(g^*f_*I^\bullet)$. Compose it with $H^q(\beta_I)$ and the two resolution comparisons. This is the asserted isomorphism for each $q\geq0$. In degree zero it is $\beta_M$, since the augmented comparison commutes with $M\to I^0$ and the degree-zero resolution identification is induced on kernels.

source.place: Tag 03LX and the injective-resolution proof of Tag 03LR; homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor); derived.tex Tags 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived), 013K

proof.text: For $a:M\to N$, choose resolutions $I,J$ as in Step 3 and lift $a$ to $t:I\to J$ by the injective-resolution lifting statement. Restriction gives a lift $h^*t$ of $h^*a$. Naturality of the ordinary comparison gives $f'_*h^*t\circ\beta_I=\beta_J\circ g^*f_*t$. Taking cohomology and using naturality of the exact-functor comparison makes the isomorphisms of Step 5 commute with $a$, because the map-via-lift statement identifies the right-derived maps with precisely these cohomology maps. Taking $a=\mathrm{id}_M$ with two different resolutions proves that their formulas agree under the canonical resolution identifications; the same statement holds for every lift, so the formula is independent of that choice. Thus the comparison is canonical and natural in $M$. All constructions are in all module sheaves; none uses quasi-coherence or a finiteness hypothesis on $f$.
